prompt: A town's population of $12{,}500$ grows by $4\%$ in one year. What is the population after that year?
hint: Growing by a percent means the town keeps everyone it had and gains a fraction more. What single multiplier describes that?

hints.text: Growing by a percent means the town keeps everyone it had and gains a fraction more. What single multiplier describes that?

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a small town: $200$ growing $10\%$ gains $20$, reaching $220$. Compute the increase, then decide whether the question wants the increase or the new total.
Find the increase first: $4\%$ of $12{,}500$ is $0.04 \times 12500 = 500$. Then add the increase to the starting population.
Adding gives $12{,}500 + 500 = 13{,}000$, so the population after the year is $13{,}000$.

learningObjective: Apply a percent increase to a large quantity.
explanation: Find the size of the increase, which is $4\%$ of the population: $0.04 \times 12500 = 500$.
Add the increase to the starting population to get $12500 + 500 = 13{,}000$.
A single multiplication gives the same result, $12500 \times 1.04 = 13{,}000$, so the population is $13{,}000$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Answer the question that was asked
steps: The increase is $500$; the new population is $13{,}000$. Both will appear as choices.
Read whether the question wants "the increase" or "the population after".
This is the single most common way to lose an otherwise trivial percent question.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: 500 — the increase alone — is the classic near-miss, and it appears among the choices.
Re-read the final clause: it asks for the population AFTER the year, so the increase must be added back: 13,000.
